To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

technological opportunities and (potential) market sizes have a significantly positive effect on the number of new molecular entities in the United States and that the effect of technological opportunities is significantly larger than the effect of (potential) markets.
the number of new molecular entities is positively affected by the size of the potential market for pharmaceuticals and by the growth of the knowledge stock of the pharmaceutical sector.
(1) market size has a positive effect on the number of new drugs and (2) the growth rate of the knowledge stock has a positive effect, too.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the pharmaceutical industry’s R&D efforts are more responsive to market size or to the technological environment.
the determinants of the industry’s R & D performance.
the question how the number of new drugs in the United States is affected by (potential) market conditions and the state of technological opportunities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both technological opportunities and market size are crucial determinants for pharmaceutical innovation.
technological opportunities, as well as potential markets, play an important role in the pharmaceutical innovation process.
technological opportunities are important, but not as important as the size of (potential) pharmaceutical markets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of new drugs in the United States depends on both the potential size of the market for the new drugs and on the technological opportunities.
the pharmaceutical industry is responsive to both market size and technological progress.
the market size and technological progress have a significant and positive effect on pharmaceutical innovation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
technological opportunities, in the form of knowledge stocks, are an important factor that should be considered in future research.
both factors are of equal importance for the pharmaceutical innovation process.
technological opportunities and market size are important determinants of pharmaceutical innovation.
